indicators.scientific_definition: Number of agents classified as unhappy in the current recorded step.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher tolerance lowers the required similarity for satisfaction, so fewer agents are classified as unhappy at equal local similarity.

indicators.scientific_rationale: The count of dissatisfaction events uses the elementary unhappy flag per agent and aggregates only over the agent axis, preserving the micro level.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of all agents classified as unhappy in the current step.

parameter_associations.rationale: A higher tolerance threshold makes more agents satisfied, reducing the unsatisfied proportion.

indicators.scientific_rationale: This indicator normalizes the elementary dissatisfaction flag over agents, allowing comparison across parameter settings without using a pre-aggregated log.

indicators.scientific_definition: Average same-group fraction among occupied Moore neighbours across agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: Stronger destination preference selects sampled vacancies with higher local similarity, raising the average local similarity after relocations.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Mean local similarity summarizes individual exposure to same-group neighbours, a core micro-level driver of satisfaction.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation of same-group fraction among occupied Moore neighbours across agents.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Dispersion across individual local similarities captures heterogeneity in agents' local social environments.

indicators.scientific_definition: Median same-group fraction among occupied Moore neighbours across agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: When destination preference is high, relocation targets are more similar, likely shifting the median exposure upward.

indicators.scientific_rationale: The median provides a robust central measure of individual local exposure that is less sensitive to extreme local similarities.

indicators.scientific_definition: Binned entropy of the distribution of agent-level local same-group similarities.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Entropy of binned local similarities measures diversity of individual local environments, indicating how mixed or sorted agents' exposures are.

indicators.scientific_definition: Average number of occupied Moore neighbours across agents.

parameter_associations.rationale: Tolerance changes which agents are unsatisfied and may alter relocation patterns, but its effect on occupied neighbour count is not monotonic.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Local occupancy affects the denominator of similarity, shaping the information available to individuals when they evaluate satisfaction.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation of occupied Moore-neighbour counts across agents.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Variation in local occupancy reflects the unevenness of crowding or vacancy distribution in agents' local neighbourhoods.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of agents that have at least one occupied different-group neighbour.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher destination preference selects more similar destination neighbourhoods, reducing contact with different-group neighbours.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Boundary agents mark local inter-group contacts; a decreasing fraction indicates stronger spatial separation.

indicators.scientific_definition: Average periodic Manhattan distance of relocations across all agents, with non-movers contributing zero.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move probability increases the number of attempted relocations, making more agents move and raising the average recorded relocation distance.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Mean relocation distance reflects how far agents move when they choose or are able to relocate.

indicators.scientific_definition: Proportion of agents that relocated during the current step.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move probability means unsatisfied agents are more likely to relocate in a given step, increasing the fraction moved.

indicators.scientific_rationale: This indicator captures the aggregate activity of elementary relocation events at the micro level.

indicators.scientific_definition: Number of agents that relocated during the current step.
indicators.entities: agents with moved flag and population size

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher move probability increases the frequency of relocation attempts, leading to more recorded moved events.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Total relocation events measure the absolute level of micro-level mobility by rescaling the moved fraction by the number of agents.

indicators.scientific_definition: Average same-group neighbour fraction at selected destinations across all agents, with non-movers contributing zero.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher destination preference directly selects the sampled vacancy with the highest local similarity, increasing destination similarity.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Destination similarity is a direct trace of the relocation choice mechanism, making it sensitive to destination_preference.

indicators.semantic_name: Agent-level correlation between local similarity and neighbour count
indicators.scientific_definition: Correlation across agents between local same-group similarity and occupied neighbour count.
indicators.entities: agent local similarity and neighbour count
indicators.scientific_rationale: This interaction-level indicator reveals how individual local similarity covaries with the amount of local occupancy.

indicators.semantic_name: Agent-level correlation between local similarity and move distance
indicators.scientific_definition: Correlation across agents between local same-group similarity and relocation distance.
indicators.entities: agent local similarity and move distance
indicators.scientific_rationale: This interaction-level indicator captures whether agents with lower local similarity tend to move farther when relocating.

indicators.scientific_definition: Number of agents with at least one occupied different-group neighbour.
indicators.entities: agents with boundary exposure and population size

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher destination preference promotes sorting into homogeneous neighbourhoods, reducing the number of agents exposed to different-group neighbours.

indicators.scientific_rationale: Counting boundary agents provides an absolute micro-level measure of inter-group contact by rescaling the boundary fraction by the number of agents.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district variation in mean local similarity
indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the mean local same-group similarity within each district.
indicators.scientific_rationale: This meso indicator captures whether average local exposure differs across real spatial districts, reflecting district-level segregation rather than individual variation alone.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district variation in mean local occupancy
indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the mean occupied neighbour count within each district.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Variation in average local occupancy across districts indicates whether crowding or vacancy is spatially organized at the meso level.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the fraction of unsatisfied agents within each district.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in dissatisfaction shows whether local dissatisfaction is spatially concentrated or spread evenly across real districts.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the proportion of boundary agents within each district.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Boundary exposure variation across districts measures how unevenly inter-group contacts are distributed across real spatial domains.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the fraction of agents that relocated during the current step.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Relocation activity variation across districts reveals which spatial domains experience the most mobility, aggregated as a meso-level distribution.

indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the mean selected destination similarity within each district.
indicators.scientific_rationale: Between-district variation in destination similarity indicates whether the relocation opportunities selected by agents differ systematically across spatial districts.

indicators.semantic_name: Between-district variation in internal similarity dispersion
indicators.scientific_definition: Standard deviation across fixed spatial districts of the within-district standard deviation of local same-group similarity.
indicators.scientific_rationale: This meso indicator captures how much the internal heterogeneity of local similarity varies across real districts, illuminating district-level mixing or sorting.

indicators.scientific_definition: Binned entropy across fixed spatial districts of the mean group label, which gives the distribution of district-level group composition.
indicators.scientific_rationale: District-level group composition entropy measures the spatial mixing of groups across real districts; higher entropy indicates more similar district compositions.

indicators.scientific_definition: Whole-grid average of same-group similarity between occupied Moore neighbours computed directly from the spatial configuration.

parameter_associations.rationale: Stronger homophilic relocation increases global spatial sorting, raising whole-grid neighbour similarity.

indicators.scientific_rationale: This global structure measure directly quantifies the degree of same-group adjacency across the entire periodic grid.

indicators.scientific_definition: Fraction of occupied grid cells contained in the largest connected occupied component of the periodic grid.
indicators.scientific_rationale: A large connected occupied component fraction indicates that most cells are part of a giant spatial cluster, a macro-level structural outcome.

indicators.scientific_definition: Number of connected occupied components in the periodic grid.
indicators.scientific_rationale: The number of connected occupied components is a global structural property reflecting spatial fragmentation across the entire system.

indicators.scientific_definition: Total unsatisfied agents divided by the number of agents in the simulation.

parameter_associations.rationale: Higher tolerance makes agents satisfied at lower similarity levels, reducing the whole-system dissatisfaction fraction.

indicators.scientific_rationale: This macro indicator aggregates all individual dissatisfaction events into a single whole-system prevalence measure at each step.

interpretation_boundary: Indicator computations are descriptive executable observables constructed only from the supplied raw-log schema and generic operators. They do not infer causal, statistical, temporal-dynamic, or intervention support, and no candidate path, edge, or prediction is implied at this phase.
